```{r rsetup,eval=TRUE,include=FALSE}
require("codecheck")
require("knitr")
require("rprojroot")
require("yaml")
require("xtable")
require("tibble")
require("readr")
options(width = 120)  # matches the 7pt code font set in the header
opts_chunk$set(cache = FALSE)

root <- find_root("codecheck.yml")
```

```{r check_sibling_template, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
## Warn if codecheck.Rmd is also present next to this file - having both
## makes it unclear which one is the canonical certificate source.
if (file.exists(file.path(root, "codecheck", "codecheck.Rmd"))) {
  warning("Both codecheck.Rmd and codecheck.qmd are present in codecheck/ - ",
          "remove one so the certificate source is unambiguous.")
}
```

```{r validate_yaml_syntax, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
## Validate YAML syntax - will stop rendering if YAML is invalid
codecheck::validate_yaml_syntax(file.path(root, "codecheck.yml"))
```

```{r check_certificate_id, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
## Check if certificate identifier is set properly and try to update from GitHub
## This will check if the certificate is a placeholder and attempt to retrieve
## the actual certificate ID from GitHub issues matching the author names

# Check if certificate is a placeholder
yml_path <- file.path(root, "codecheck.yml")
if (codecheck::is_placeholder_certificate(yml_path)) {
  message("CERTIFICATE ID NOT SET")

  # Try to automatically retrieve and update certificate from GitHub
  result <- codecheck::update_certificate_from_github(
    yml_file = yml_path,
    issue_state = "open",
    apply_update = FALSE  # Set to TRUE to automatically update
  )

  if (!is.null(result$certificate) && result$certificate != "") {
    message("\n✓ Certificate found! To apply the update, run:")
    message("\n  codecheck::update_certificate_from_github(apply_update = TRUE)")
    message("\nOr manually update codecheck.yml with certificate: ", result$certificate)
  } else {
    message("\nℹ No matching certificate found in GitHub issues.")
    message("You may need to manually set the certificate identifier in codecheck.yml")
  }
}
```

```{r manifest, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
metadata <- codecheck::codecheck_metadata(root)
manifest <- metadata$manifest

dest_dir <- file.path(root, "codecheck", "outputs")
## Create the outputs directory if missing
if (!dir.exists(dest_dir) ) {
  dir.create(dest_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

manifest_df <- codecheck::list_manifest_files(root, metadata, dest_dir)
```

```{r validate_crossref, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
## Validate metadata against CrossRef and ORCID metadata - will fail rendering on mismatch
## Set strict = FALSE or remove this chunk if you want to skip validation
##
## ORCID name checks first try the authenticated ORCID API, then automatically
## fall back to the public, unauthenticated ORCID API for records whose name
## is publicly visible - so most checks work without any ORCID setup at all.
## skip_on_auth_error only matters if BOTH lookups fail for a record (e.g. no
## network access, or the record's name is not public); it is enabled below
## so a fresh workspace always renders even in that case.
validation_result <- codecheck::validate_contents_references(
  yml_file = file.path(root, "codecheck.yml"),
  strict = TRUE
  , skip_on_auth_error = TRUE
)
```

```{r print_title, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
## The certificate title/subtitle depend on `metadata`, computed above from
## codecheck.yml - unlike R Markdown, Quarto's knitr engine does not evaluate
## inline `r` code inside a document's YAML metadata blocks, so the title
## cannot be set dynamically via YAML here. It is instead emitted directly as
## LaTeX, using the same \title/\subtitle/\maketitle commands pandoc's
## title-block metadata would otherwise have produced.
cat(sprintf("\\title{%s}\n", paste("CODECHECK certificate", metadata$certificate)))
cat(sprintf("\\subtitle{%s}\n", codecheck:::as_latex_url(metadata$report)))
cat("\\maketitle\n")
```

```{r codecheck_logo, echo=FALSE,results='asis'}
codecheck::latex_codecheck_logo()
```

```{r validate_certificate, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
## Validate certificate and display warning if placeholder, or if the
## report DOI is a Zenodo concept DOI instead of a version-specific DOI
## Set strict = TRUE to fail rendering if certificate is a placeholder
## Set display_warning = FALSE to suppress the warning box in PDF output
codecheck::validate_certificate_for_rendering(
  yml_file = file.path(root, "codecheck.yml"),
  strict = FALSE,           # Set to TRUE to fail rendering
  display_warning = TRUE    # Set to FALSE to hide warning in PDF
)
```

```{r summary_metadata, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
codecheck::latex_summary_of_metadata(metadata)
```

```{r summary_manifest, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
codecheck::latex_summary_of_manifest(metadata, manifest_df, root)
```

\clearpage

# CODECHECKER notes

```{r git_sha, echo=FALSE}
gitInfo <- codecheck::get_git_info(root)
```

`r gitInfo`

The code and data used for this check are available in the
[OSF record](https://osf.io/9v3rh/).

The code (`analysis code.R`, written in R) and data (`data experts.csv`,
`data laypeople.csv`) were run unmodified, with the working directory set to
the folder containing the data. The script was run from the top up to and
including the definition of `model4b` (line 813). The bootstrapped
`confint()` calls were skipped, as they are not needed for Tables S1-S4. The
reproduced output of `summary()` for each model was saved to a text file and
compared with the corresponding table in `supplemental materials.pdf`.

**Result: Tables S1-S4 were reproduced with small numerical differences.**
The comparisons below show last-digit differences of up to 0.001 in some
reported coefficients and in the Table S1 intercept p-value (.506 reproduced
versus .507 published). Their cause has not been established; rounding or
truncation may account for some differences. The comparisons shown do not
change the statistical significance of the reported effects. This check
covers these four tables, excluding the bootstrapped confidence intervals,
rather than the complete analysis workflow.

| Table | Reproduced by | Model | Outcome | Result |
|-------|---------------|-------|---------|--------|
| S1 | `summary(model3a)` | `glmer`, binomial | Consciousness attribution | Reproduced |
| S2 | `summary(model3b)` | `glmer`, binomial | Emotion attribution | Reproduced (differences of up to 0.001) |
| S3 | `summary(model4a)` | `lmer` | Confidence, consciousness | Reproduced |
| S4 | `summary(model4b)` | `lmer` | Confidence, emotion | Reproduced |

Evidence (reproduced estimate / SE / p vs. published b / SE / p):

| Table | Predictor | Reproduced | Published |
|-------|-----------|------------|-----------|
| S1 | Intercept | -0.833 / 1.253 / .506 | -0.832 / 1.253 / .507 |
| S1 | Veg*n diet | 1.689 / 0.676 / .012 | 1.689 / 0.676 / .012 |
| S2 | Conservative | -0.128 / 0.048 / .007 | -0.128 / 0.048 / .007 |
| S2 | Veg*n diet | 1.820 / 0.519 / < .001 | 1.819 / 0.519 / < .001 |
| S3 | Intercept | 3.400 / 0.237 / < .001 | 3.400 / 0.237 / < .001 |
| S3 | Religiosity | 0.131 / 0.082 / .109 | 0.131 / 0.082 / .109 |
| S4 | Age | 0.005 / 0.002 / .032 | 0.004 / 0.002 / .032 |
| S4 | Conservative | -0.029 / 0.013 / .024 | -0.029 / 0.013 / .024 |
| S4 | Religiosity | 0.253 / 0.075 / < .001 | 0.253 / 0.075 / < .001 |

The full `summary()` output of each model is included in the manifest files
below (`table_S1_model3a.txt` to `table_S4_model4b.txt`).

R printed a convergence warning (max|grad| = 0.003, tolerance 0.002) while
running the script; the reproduced estimates still match the published values.
The script runs in about 20 seconds on my laptop (excluding the bootstrapped
confidence intervals).

## Recommendations

I suggest to the authors to consider the following suggestions for their next publication or workflow:

- Add a `README` listing the required R packages (and versions) and stating that the script must be run from the folder containing the data.
- Replace the spaces in file names (`analysis code.R`, `data experts.csv`) to make them easier to use from the command line.
- Label each `summary()` call in the script with the table it produces (e.g. `# Table S1`).
- The line `ci <- cbind(exp(fixef(...), exp(confint.merMod(...))))` has a misplaced parenthesis, so the odds ratios are not computed as intended; consider fixing it.

# About CODECHECK

This certificate confirms that the codechecker could independently
reproduce the results of a computational analysis given the data and
code from a third party.  A CODECHECK does not check whether the
original computation analysis is correct.  However, as all materials
required for the reproduction are freely available by following the
links in this document, the reader can then study for themselves the
code and data.
